chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

No two groups of the people of falsehood ever confronted each other at all except that the victory was with the better one of them, while the other way round (opposite) being for the people of Al-Islam.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in how victory is determined among the people of falsehood versus the people of Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of 'fawz' (victory) by distinguishing between relative excellence within a flawed system and absolute excellence within the true faith. Shia scholars often interpret 'ahsan' (better) in the context of the people of falsehood as referring to their internal coherence or merit, while victory for the people of Islam is reserved for those who embody the highest degree of spiritual and moral perfection. This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on both outward conformity and inward sincerity as criteria for divine support.
